title.narrative: Cash Plus support for Draught affected Communities in Afgoye-Enhancing lifesaving food security through cash and sustainable farming.

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtThrough this project, Action Sustainability Improvement Programs (ASIP) will ensure immediate and intermediate access to food for crisis-affected and food-insecure households in Afgooye Villages, as outlined in the SHF Reserve Allocation 2025. This initiative aims to support approximately 2,573 households, comprising 1,261 male and 1,312 female beneficiaries, potentially reaching a total of 15,438 individuals based on an average household size of six in Somalia. The project is designed to align fully with the SHF Reserve Allocation 2025 and adheres to the Food Security Cluster guidelines, ensuring that all interventions meet established standards for effectiveness and quality.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtUtilizing a Cash Plus approach, the project will integrate unconditional cash transfers (UCT), and emergency agricultural inputs to ensure vulnerable households’ immediate availability and access to food while also enabling them to produce locally and secure a harvest/ food stock. with support for livelihood restoration activities, particularly focusing on fast-maturing food production. Households will be identified through a vulnerability-based targeting (VBT) strategy, enhancing inclusivity and ensuring that the most disadvantaged groups receive the needed support. ASIP's past experience has demonstrated the effectiveness of VBT in improving representation, which successfully increased minority clan inclusion from 25% to 35% and the participation of persons with disabilities (PWD) from 7% to 10% compared to the previous year.ltbrgtThe project will specifically focus on underserved riverine villages of ltbgtMareerey, Tawakal and Balgurelt/bgt Villages where marginalized communities are grappling with the most severe levels of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM), currently recorded at 16.4% in Afgooye. In prioritizing assistance, the project will also emphasize support for returning internally displaced persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable groups. UCT will serve as a crucial entry point to bolster food security for these households.ltbrgtIn a bid to foster community involvement, ASIP will intentionally engage targeted households through inclusive feedback mechanisms, ensuring that beneficiaries have a voice in the assistance process. Inputs for agricultural activities will be determined in consultation with local farmers, guaranteeing that communities can effectively cultivate a minimum of an acre. A carefully curated mix of cereal and vegetable seeds will be distributed, specifically adapted to the riverine environment, thus improving access to a nutritious and balanced diet.ltbrgtGender and protection mainstreaming will be fundamental throughout the project. All proposed villages are home to ethnic minorities within Afgooye, and ASIP is committed to ensuring that at least 10% of UCT recipients are Gender based Violence (GBV), as identified and referred by partner agencies through protection and GBV working groups.ltbrgtFurthermore, ASIP will actively collaborate in both intra- and inter-agency referral systems, particularly focusing on protection, health, and nutrition services to create a comprehensive support network for beneficiaries. Access barriers, service quality, and protection risks will be continuously monitored through client satisfaction surveys, call center data, and community consultations, allowing for adaptive management of the project based on real-time feedback.ltbrgtTo reinforce accountability and safeguard against abuses, the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be promoted through targeted information sessions, which aim to educate households on recognizing and reporting SEA cases. This multifaceted approach not only aims to meet immediate needs but also seeks to empower communities, fostering resilience and dignity amid challenging conditions.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
